label: The cheapest one-lineage refusal has an existing precedent in fanout-run.cjs: the stopPolicy=max-iterations guard at the lineage-expansion boundary (3396-3406) throws inputError, which surfaces as {status:error, code:INPUT_VALIDATION} with a non-zero exit from the top-level catch.

A schema-level executors minimum of two is the expensive variant and the wrong layer: parseFanoutConfig is a shared contract whose unit fixtures rely on single-entry arrays and count expansion; the policy is a caller rule and belongs at the CLI boundary.

A hard refusal cannot break a legitimate workflow path: production callers pass multi-lineage config.fanout_json (research YAML 225, review confirm YAML 210, council via orchestrate-session) and fanout-salvage does not build executor lists; the blast radius is three stress fixtures that would need count: 2.

A guard inside fanout-run.cjs is inert in a dispatched child: fanout-run is the parent-side runner, the child prompt forbids nested dispatch, and nothing in a lineage calls it, so the check costs nothing per runtime and never meets a sandbox.

The hook option costs six separate runtime mechanisms (Claude/Codex/Cursor/Devin shims, an in-process Pi extension, an OpenCode plugin), all prompt-time context injection, spread over seven runtime agent directories; the deep-research capability matrix records hookBootstrap true for one of the two runtimes it tracks.

A runner that owns the single-executor loop is a new subsystem, not a wrapper: no runtime script parses the auto YAML's step blocks, render-command-contract.cjs renders command contracts from a manifest, and the driver is 267 lines that rebind YAML command blocks and call five runtime scripts in order.

A correctly walked fan-out run does write packet-level config.status: complete, because step_update_config_status sits in phase_synthesis with no skip_when and fan-out jumps into phase_synthesis; the status field is therefore a valid post-hoc discriminator, but a legitimate early stop also leaves it initialized, so it cannot be a hard gate.

A gateway-hosted gate is the highest-blast-radius candidate and cannot stop a run: the append gateway refuses before the ledger and records refusals best-effort in gateway-refusals.jsonl while every lineage and all three loop types call it, so a new precondition changes the record stream rather than the route.

The documentation candidate survives only as the text a session reads at the decision point: it is the same class of control the incident defeated, but it is the only candidate that reaches the reader before the first dispatch, and it costs one sentence in each of two existing command docs.

reason: Wrong layer: parseFanoutConfig is the shared parse contract and single-entry arrays are used across its fixtures for reasons unrelated to the caller policy.

direction: Append-gateway precondition requiring a live lock
reason: Fires on the incident path but reaches every lineage, mode and crash-resume, and the refusal path is designed not to change the CLI result.
Six runtime-specific adapters delivering prompt-time context; reproduces the prose control at maximum maintenance cost.
